claims.text: The platform's own derived deviation block measures the excess on this trip at 7.36 km against an optimal route of 6.4 km, which is 115% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass: the excess is greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms and greater than 20% of optimal. Because it is also greater than 50% of optimal, the deviation is additionally MATERIAL. The governing distance for the threshold test is gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 13.76 km — POL-RD-01 expressly forbids citing the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 13.8 km, and the rider does not rely on it.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. The artifacts describe the same trip: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00109, and the pickup/start timestamps agree (accepted 18:17:02, started 18:21:10, first GPS fix 18:21:10). The excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace — 207 fixes at 10 s intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to name a specific artifact and a specific clause; a general assertion that the rider asked for a stop does not by itself fix the quantum exonerated.

No traffic advisory exists for this trip. EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING — weight 0.0, issue codes MISSING_ARTIFACT — and carries no payload, so no road, expressway segment or junction can be named under POL-RD-03 as a segment the optimal route traverses. The rider states the impairment plainly: this artifact has no weight and cannot carry a fact, but its absence is citable, and it means POL-RD-03 can exonerate nothing here.

The rider accepts that MSG-00109-001 asks the driver to 'stop at jurong point first' and that the message carries a resolved waypoint_hint at VEN-JURONG-POINT, with the driver agreeing at MSG-00109-002, so POL-RD-04 is engaged. But POL-RD-04 exonerates only 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor', and the record contains no computation of that leg: trip_record.amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, there is no amendment timestamp for POL-RD-05 to run on, and no derived block measures a detour-adjusted excess. An instruction to make a five-minute stop at one venue does not, without more, price the whole 115% excess out of the claim, and the driver bears the burden of showing the reduced figure he says applies.

On the METERED fare the POL-RD-02 arithmetic gives: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 6.4 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.0 surge, plus 0.80 platform fee, plus 0 ERP and surcharges, plus waiting_time_fee 0.00, less promo 0 = 12.52 + 0.80 = 13.32. Charged_total is 21.32, so the refund is 8.00. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 37.5% of the amount charged, far below the 90% that would convert it to a full refund — so the rider's claim is for a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.00. The platform's own fare model reaches the identical figure (refund.payable 8.00), which the rider adopts.

The rider was metered time_fare of 9.52 for 34.0 charged minutes against an optimal_duration_min of 14.0, and the fare carries waiting_time_fee of 0.00 — the minutes spent at the pickup point were billed as trip time, not as a separate waiting charge. POL-RD-02 prices the recomputed fare at the optimal duration and then adds fare_breakdown.waiting_time_fee, which here is zero. There is no properly chargeable waiting line to add back into the recomputation, and the rider should not be asked to pay again in the waiting column for time already priced out of the distance-and-time lines.

The extra corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08 does not bite on this rider. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0 — nowhere near the 4-or-more claims with 1-or-fewer substantiated that the clause names — and the requirement applies only to excesses below 30%, whereas this excess is 115%. The rider's claim also does not rest on assertion alone: it rests on the same platform telemetry the fare was billed from.

The MATERIAL finding under POL-RD-01 requires the driver_profile check in POL-RD-06, and the rider states the result honestly: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 511 — no pattern is established on the trailing-90-day counters, and the rider does not seek the POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift. The materiality finding itself stands on this trip's own evidence, which is all POL-RD-06 permits it to rest on.

The driver's statement that he drove 13.8 km while the receipt shows 9.6 km is arithmetically right — distance_charged_km is 9.60 against a trace_distance_km of 13.76 — but POL-RD-04's compensation limb is discretionary ('may be granted'), and if it is granted at all it is a driver payment that POL-GEN-03 makes INDEPENDENT of the rider's refund and never netted against it. It cannot be used to reduce or offset the SGD 8.00 the rider is owed on the mileage and time actually contested.

The rider asked for this stop in her own words. MSG-00109-001, sent at 18:22:06 — 56 seconds after the meter started at 18:21:10 — reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'. POL-RD-04 is satisfied limb by limb: the instruction is from the rider (sender RIDER); it was sent before the vehicle left the optimal corridor and in any event well inside the clause's 3-minute allowance; and 'stop at Jurong Point first' is the very example the clause gives of a place named specifically enough to act on. The rider's dispute narrative — that the driver 'anyhow drove' — is contradicted by her own message one minute into the trip.

The trace corroborates the instruction exactly as POL-RD-04 requires. The platform resolved the waypoint from the message text at ingest — the waypoint_hint on MSG-00109-001 is 'Jurong Point, PHV Pickup Point, 1 Jurong West Central 2', venue_id VEN-JURONG-POINT — and the admissibility assessment on EV-GPS-00109 records the vehicle stationary 38 m from that point for 366 seconds. 38 m is far inside the clause's 200 m proximity test, and the 366-second dwell matches the rider's own '5 min' estimate. This is not a case of a chat request the trace never approaches.

POL-RD-04 excludes the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor before POL-RD-01 is applied, and POL-RD-01 expressly assesses materiality on the excess REMAINING after that adjustment. The whole of the measured 7.36 km excess lies on the diversion the rider created: the vehicle left the optimal corridor for the requested waypoint, sat there while she ran her errand, and then ran on to Bukit Batok. Nothing that survives the exclusion remains, both POL-RD-01 establishment tests fail, and the rider's claim is not supported — the present state, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, stands under POL-GEN-03.

Even taking the excess at its measured material 115%, POL-RD-06's driver_profile check comes back clean. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 511: neither limb is met (0 is below 3, and 0/511 = 0.00 is below the 0.05 ratio with 40 or more trips). No pattern is established, so there is no POL-RD-06(b) uplift to FULL_REFUND to consider and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral to record. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day field this clause asks for, and the driver does not rely on it.

The rider cannot escape POL-RD-04 by attacking the trace. EV-GPS-00109 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0: 207 fixes, 100.0% coverage, a 10-second sample interval, no gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) fires, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes, the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is never engaged, and the rider's POL-RD-08(b) threshold showing rests on an unimpaired trace — which is exactly why the driver must, and does, answer it on the merits.

Separately, and standing on its own, the driver was under-billed and POL-RD-04 provides for it. The fare_breakdown bills the rider for 9.60 km while the trace records 13.76 km — a shortfall of 4.16 km, well past the 1.0 km trigger. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre, 4.16 x 0.75 = SGD 3.12, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 as SGD 3.15, comfortably inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. The platform's own note on EV-FARE-00109 records that distance_charged_km of 9.60 is below both the trace and actual distance and that the driver was under-billed.

There is nothing to correct under POL-RD-09 on this trip. The fare_breakdown carries erp_gantries as an empty set, tolls_erp of 0.00 and an airport_surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no off-route or phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge for the rider to recover. POL-RD-09(3) confirms the position: where the detour was rider-caused under POL-RD-04, no ERP refund is due.

EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING — weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — and I disclose that impairment rather than present the artifact as usable. Its absence is itself citable: no traffic advisory exists for this trip, so there is no external road-condition exoneration under POL-RD-03 to weigh, and none is needed, because the assessor records the detour as explained by the rider's own instruction and not by any road condition. The driver's POL-RD-04 case requires only the chat log, GPS trace, trip record and fare breakdown, all present and complete at weight 1.0.

The POL-RD-08 burden shifted to the driver once the rider showed matching trip identity and a threshold excess, and the driver discharges it by pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause: EV-CHAT-00109 and the rider-requested-detour exoneration in POL-RD-04. This is not the POL-RD-10(7) deadlock of mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength — the place the rider named in the chat is the place the trace shows the vehicle stopping — so no mandatory escalation is triggered and the case is decidable on the papers.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the rider's route-deviation claim is not supported, and the driver is owed a small under-billing payment of SGD 3.15.

ROUTE DEVIATION. On the platform's own measurement the trip ran 13.76 km (gps_trace.trace_distance_km) against an optimal 6.4 km — an excess of 7.36 km, 115% of optimal. That would clear both POL-RD-01 tests and be a MATERIAL deviation. It is, however, fully excused by POL-RD-04. The chat log carries the rider's own message MSG-00109-001, sent 18:22:06 — 56 seconds after the meter started at 18:21:10: 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'. It comes from the rider, sits well inside the clause's three-minute window, and names the very place the clause gives as its example. The waypoint the platform resolved from that text is Jurong Point PHV Pickup Point (VEN-JURONG-POINT), and the GPS trace shows the vehicle stationary 38 m from it for 366 seconds — inside the 200 m proximity test. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 207 fixes at 10 s, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0. The whole measured excess lies on that diversion — the vehicle left the optimal corridor for Jurong Point and rejoined it on the run to Bukit Batok — so once the excess between leaving and rejoining is excluded, nothing remains that passes POL-RD-01 and no deviation is established. No POL-RD-02 recomputation therefore runs, and the rider's figure of an SGD 8.00 partial refund (recomputed_fare 13.32 against charged_total 21.32) is the arithmetic of a deviation that is fully excused; it does not issue. The rider's point that the record contains no stored computation of the excluded leg does not change this: POL-RD-05 never engages (pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null, so no re-quote was required), POL-RD-04 calls for no stored figure, and the trace together with the resolved waypoint shows the entire diversion is the stop she asked for.

DRIVER COMPENSATION. The fare billed the rider for 9.60 km (distance_charged_km) while the trace records 13.76 km — a shortfall of 4.16 km, above the 1.0 km trigger in POL-RD-04. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is 4.16 x 0.75 = SGD 3.12, rounded UP to SGD 3.15, inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. The driver is entitled to SGD 3.15. This is a payment to the driver, independent of any rider refund and never netted against one; the rider's own charge stands.

OTHER CLAUSES. POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and carries no payload, though the case does not need it — both advocates disclosed that impairment. POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is clean (deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 511), so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral; the claim correctly uses the trailing-90-day counter and does not rely on lifetime prior_deviation_flags. POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct — no ERP gantries, no tolls, no airport surcharge — and POL-RD-09(3) gives no ERP refund on a rider-caused detour. POL-RD-08's extra corroboration requirement does not bite (deviation_claims_60d 1, substantiated 0, and the excess is 115%, not below 30%). No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trace is not impaired, trip identifiers and timestamps agree, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or incomplete artifact, and no charge line lacks a counterpart. Confidence is 0.85, above the 0.70 floor.

To the rider and the driver. The trip did deviate: the optimal route Clementi to Bukit Batok is 6.4 km, the GPS trace records 13.76 km, an excess of 7.36 km, which is 115% of optimal. That passes both POL-RD-01 establishment tests and is MATERIAL, and I accept it. But the deviation is the rider's, and POL-RD-04 excuses it. The rider's own message MSG-00109-001, sent at 18:22:06 — 56 seconds after the meter started at 18:21:10 — reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', and the platform resolved the waypoint Jurong Point (VEN-JURONG-POINT) from that text; the driver agreed at 18:22:31. The GPS trace — complete, 207 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps — puts the vehicle stationary 38 m from that waypoint for 366 seconds, inside the clause's 200 m corroboration test. The instruction came from the rider, inside the 3-minute window, and 'stop at Jurong Point first' is the clause's own example of a place named specifically enough to act on. POL-RD-04 excludes the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor; the route actually driven is the route to Jurong Point and on to Bukit Batok, so the whole 7.36 km excess is that detour, nothing survives the exclusion, no deviation remains, and the rider's refund is nil. The rider's advocate is right that the raw excess is 115% and MATERIAL, but wrong that POL-RD-02 produces SGD 8.00 here: POL-RD-04 requires the detour excess to be excluded before POL-RD-02 runs, and once it is there is no deviation to refund against. I also reject his submission that the exoneration is unquantified: POL-RD-04 runs on the chat log, the resolved waypoint and the trace, all present at full weight, and the stored amended-route field he points to is POL-RD-05's requirement, not engaged here because no endpoint was amended (amended_optimal_distance_km is null and no amendment timestamp exists). The claimed refund of 8.00 is not made; charged_total 21.32 and recomputed_fare 13.32 are recorded, but the 8.00 difference is the exonerated detour and the charge of SGD 21.32 stands. The waiting-time point is moot: the fare carries waiting_time_fee 0.00, so there is no waiting line to add back. On the driver's side, the fare breakdown bills 9.60 km while the trace records 13.76 km — a 4.16 km shortfall, past the 1.0 km trigger. Under POL-RD-04's separate limb I grant the driver DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 4.16 x SGD 0.75 = SGD 3.12, rounded up to SGD 3.15, inside the SGD 15.00 cap. This is a platform-funded payment to the driver; it is independent of any rider refund, is not netted against the rider, and leaves the rider's charge standing. No traffic advisory exists: EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; its absence is citable and means POL-RD-03 can exonerate nothing, but it carries no fact, and this ruling rests on no impaired artifact. Nothing arises under POL-RD-09: the fare carries no ERP gantries, no tolls and no airport surcharge. POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is clean — deviation_flags_90d 0 across completed_trips_90d 511 — so there is no repeat pattern, no uplift to FULL_REFUND and no driver-conduct referral. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context-only under POL-GEN-01 and is not a ground of decision; the only surviving claim that mentions it correctly disclaims it. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trace is complete and unimpaired, the trip identifiers and timestamps agree across trip record, trace and fare, and confidence is above the 0.70 floor. The case is decidable on the papers. Ruling: DRIVER_COMPENSATION, amount SGD 3.15, driver compensation SGD 3.15, confidence 0.90.

To both parties. The platform's measurements are accepted as they stand: the trip ran 13.76 km (GPS trace EV-GPS-00109) against an optimal route of 6.4 km (trip record EV-TRIP-00109), an excess of 7.36 km and 115% of optimal. On those figures alone the excess is MATERIAL under POL-RD-01. But the excess does not survive POL-RD-04.

POL-RD-04 applies limb by limb. (a) The instruction is the rider's own: MSG-00109-001 on the chat log (EV-CHAT-00109), 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', sender RIDER. (b) It was sent at 18:22:06, 56 seconds after the trip started at 18:21:10 — inside the clause's 3-minute allowance. (c) It names a place specifically enough to act on, and the clause's own example is 'stop at Jurong Point first'; it carries the platform-resolved waypoint_hint for Jurong Point (VEN-JURONG-POINT), and the driver agreed at MSG-00109-002. The GPS trace corroborates it as the clause requires: the vehicle was stationary 38 m from that waypoint for 366 seconds, well inside the 200 m proximity test. The whole of the 7.36 km excess is the excursion the rider asked for — the trace distance is the Clementi-to-Jurong-Point-to-Bukit-Batok route, and its excess over the direct 6.4 km optimal is precisely that diversion. Excluding it leaves no excess; both POL-RD-01 establishment tests fail; no deviation is established. The rider's narrative that the driver 'anyhow drove' is contradicted by her own message one minute into the trip and by her 'coming down now' at 18:35:40 after the stop. The rider's waiting-time point (time_fare 9.52 for 34.0 charged minutes against an optimal duration of 14.0, waiting_time_fee 0.00) is answered the same way: the time was her own requested stop, and the fare stands. The POL-RD-02 arithmetic the rider offers (charged_total 21.32, recomputed_fare 13.32, refund 8.00) only runs if a deviation survives, and none does. I make no refund; the charge of 21.32 stands and the contested 12.00 is not supported. The rider's own profile claim under POL-RD-08 (deviation_claims_60d 1, substantiated 0) is accepted and changes nothing.

The driver is separately under-billed. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00109) bills distance_charged_km of 9.60 while the trace records 13.76 km — a shortfall of 4.16 km, past the 1.0 km trigger in POL-RD-04. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre, 4.16 x 0.75 = SGD 3.12, rounded up to SGD 3.15, inside the SGD 15.00 cap. I grant DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 3.15. Under POL-GEN-03 this is independent of the rider's position and is not netted against anything, and on a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling amount_sgd carries the same figure.

The rider's objection that no artifact computes the detour leg does not change the result: POL-RD-04's exclusion runs on the record's own figures, and the amended-endpoint figures the rider looks for belong to POL-RD-05, which has no application because no endpoint was amended.

On the remaining clauses: the rider's POL-RD-08 identity-and-threshold showing is made out, and the driver discharges the shifted burden with a specific artifact and a specific clause (EV-CHAT-00109 and POL-RD-04). EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING — weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so it carries no fact and POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing; that is immaterial here because the detour is rider-caused, not road-caused. The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is clean (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 511), so there is no POL-RD-06(b) uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and nothing rests on it. POL-RD-09 produces nothing: no ERP gantries, no tolls, no airport surcharge, so no pass-through or billing-integrity correction arises. The trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and is not impaired under POL-RD-07 (207 fixes, 10-second interval, 100% coverage, max gap 0.0), so no POL-RD-10(3) escalation and no POL-GEN-02(2) discount is engaged. No escalation trigger fires. Confidence is capped at 1.0 by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding facts (the GPS trace, the chat log, the trip record and the fare breakdown); I record 0.90.

Addressed to both parties.

Rider — your route-deviation complaint is not supported, and no refund issues. The trip telemetry does show the raw deviation you describe: the GPS trace records 13.76 km against the platform's optimal 6.4 km, an excess of 7.36 km (115%), which is a MATERIAL deviation under POL-RD-01. But the cause is your own instruction. Your message MSG-00109-001, sent at 18:22:06 — 56 seconds after the meter started at 18:21:10 — reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', and it carries the platform-resolved waypoint for Jurong Point (VEN-JURONG-POINT). The driver accepted it at MSG-00109-002 ('ok can, i wait at the phv pickup point'), and the GPS trace shows the vehicle stationary 38 m from that waypoint for 366 seconds — well inside POL-RD-04's 200 m proximity test, and your request is the very example the clause gives. POL-RD-04 therefore excludes the detour distance before POL-RD-01 is applied; the whole of the measured excess is that Jurong Point excursion, so no excess over the threshold remains and no deviation survives. I have noted your point that the record stores no separate figure for the excluded leg (amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null), but that stored re-quote belongs to POL-RD-05 (endpoint relocation), not POL-RD-04, and the exclusion here is answered by the trace itself. For transparency, had the detour not been yours the POL-RD-02 arithmetic would have been charged_total 21.32 less recomputed_fare 13.32 = a refund of 8.00; that refund does not issue, and the fare stands as charged (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), so no NO_ACTION 'restore' issue arises.

Driver — the same clause that exonerates the detour also compensates you for the distance you drove but did not bill. The fare breakdown charges 9.60 km while the GPS trace records 13.76 km, a shortfall of 4.16 km, above POL-RD-04's 1.0 km trigger.
